name: Chair Squat
cues: Sit back toward the chair like you're about to sit down, then stand back up.
Keep your weight through your heels, not your toes.
Tap the chair lightly with your hips, don't fully sit, then rise.
commonMistake: Letting the knees cave inward as you stand up.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
cues: Hold one dumbbell close to your chest with both hands.
Bend your knees and hips to lower down, like sitting into a low chair.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up.
commonMistake: Rising onto the toes instead of pushing through the whole foot.

name: Seated Leg Extension (with band)
cues: Sit tall in a sturdy chair with the band looped around one ankle and anchored under the other foot.
Straighten one knee slowly until your leg is extended, then lower with control.
Keep your back against the chair the whole time.
commonMistake: Kicking the leg out fast instead of moving slowly.

name: Standing Hip Hinge
cues: This is a hip hinge — bending forward from your hips, not your lower back, with a soft bend in the knees.
Reach your hips backward as your chest tips forward, like closing a car door with your hip.
Come back up by squeezing your glutes (the muscles in your buttocks) to standing.
commonMistake: Rounding the lower back instead of bending at the hips.

jargonGloss.hip hinge: bending forward from the hips while keeping the back straight

name: Dumbbell Hip Hinge (Romanian Deadlift)
cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
This is a hip hinge — push your hips back and let the weights slide down toward your shins, chest tipping forward.
Squeeze your glutes (buttock muscles) to stand back up tall.
commonMistake: Bending the knees too much so it becomes a squat instead of a hinge.

jargonGloss.hip hinge: bending forward from the hips while keeping the back straight

name: Seated Hip Hinge (chair-supported, with band)
cues: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair with the band under both feet, one end in each hand.
This is a hip hinge — fold forward from your hips with a flat back, then pull the band as you sit back up tall.
Move slowly in both directions.
commonMistake: Rounding the shoulders forward instead of keeping the chest lifted.

jargonGloss.hip hinge: bending forward from the hips while keeping the back straight

name: Wall Push-Up
cues: Stand an arm's length from a wall, hands flat on the wall at shoulder height.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then push back.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
commonMistake: Letting the hips sag or pike instead of staying in a straight line.

name: Incline Push-Up (counter or sturdy table)
cues: Place both hands on a sturdy counter or table, feet back so your body is at an angle.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the counter, then push back up.
Keep your body in a straight line, don't let your hips drop.
commonMistake: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides instead of at a slight angle.

name: Seated Chest Press (with band)
cues: Sit tall with the band wrapped around your upper back, one end in each hand at chest height.
Push both hands forward until your arms are extended, then return with control.
Keep your back flat against the chair.
commonMistake: Leaning forward to help push instead of using the chest and arms.

name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
cues: Sit tall in a sturdy chair, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Press both dumbbells up until your arms are straight, without arching your back.
Lower with control back to shoulder height.
commonMistake: Arching the lower back to help press the weight up.

name: Doorframe Row
cues: Hold both sides of a sturdy doorframe, feet back, leaning your weight back with straight arms.
Pull your chest toward the doorframe by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly to the starting lean.
commonMistake: Pulling with just the arms instead of squeezing the shoulder blades together first.

name: Seated Row (with band)
cues: Sit tall with legs extended, band looped around your feet, one end in each hand.
Pull your elbows straight back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly, keeping your back tall the whole time.
commonMistake: Rounding the shoulders forward at the start instead of sitting tall.

name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row (chair-supported)
cues: Rest one hand and knee on a sturdy chair, holding a dumbbell in the other hand.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your ribs, leading with your elbow.
Lower slowly back down with control.
commonMistake: Twisting the torso to lift the weight instead of keeping the back flat.

name: Seated Marching (core)
cues: Sit tall toward the front edge of a sturdy chair, hands holding the sides for support.
Lift one knee up toward your chest, then lower it, alternating sides.
Keep your back tall instead of leaning back as you lift.
commonMistake: Leaning backward to help lift the knee instead of sitting tall.

name: Suitcase Carry
cues: Hold one dumbbell (or a loaded bag) at your side, standing tall.
Walk a short, clear path keeping your shoulders level and torso upright.
Switch sides halfway through.
commonMistake: Leaning sideways away from the weight instead of standing tall.

name: Farmer's Carry (loaded bag)
cues: Hold a loaded bag or bags in each hand, standing tall.
Walk a short, clear path with your shoulders back and steps steady.
Set the bags down with control if you feel unsteady.
commonMistake: Rushing the steps instead of walking at a controlled, steady pace.

name: Supported Single-Leg Stance
cues: Stand behind a sturdy chair, holding the back of it with both hands.
Lift one foot slightly off the floor and hold, keeping your hips level.
Switch feet after the set time.
commonMistake: Gripping the chair so tightly that the shoulders creep up toward the ears.

name: Tandem Stance (heel-to-toe, supported)
cues: Stand next to a wall or counter for light fingertip support.
Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toe.
Hold the position, then switch which foot is in front.
commonMistake: Looking down at the feet instead of straight ahead, which throws off balance.

name: Seated Hip Hinge (chair, no equipment)
cues: Sit tall on the front half of a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor.
This is a hip hinge — fold forward from your hips with a flat back, sliding your hands down your thighs toward your knees.
Squeeze your glutes (buttock muscles) and press your feet down to sit back up tall.
commonMistake: Rounding the upper back and letting the chin drop instead of keeping the chest lifted.

jargonGloss.hip hinge: bending forward from the hips while keeping the back straight

name: Seated Knee Extension (no equipment)
cues: Sit tall in a sturdy chair with your back supported and both feet flat.
Slowly straighten one knee until the leg is out in front of you, and pause for a moment.
Lower the foot back down slowly, then switch legs.
commonMistake: Swinging the leg up quickly instead of lifting and lowering under control.

name: Seated Palm Press (no equipment)
cues: Sit tall with your back against the chair and press your palms together in front of your chest.
Push your hands into each other firmly and hold for a slow count of five.
Relax for a moment between each press.
commonMistake: Holding your breath while pressing — keep breathing steadily throughout.

name: Seated Shoulder Blade Squeeze (no equipment)
cues: Sit tall with your arms bent and elbows tucked near your sides.
Draw your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, as if pinching something between them.
Hold for a slow count of three, then release with control.
commonMistake: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears instead of drawing them back and down.
